bullets.title: The Top Idea in Your Mind
bullets.creator: Paul Graham

bullets.title: Speaking With The Mind | Neuralink
bullets.creator: Neuralink
bullets.note: Prepare to tear up in the best way possible. This video really got me. The description: “Terry was diagnosed with bulbar-onset amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in 2024. While he is still able to move his mouth and body, his speech has become impaired to the point where his loved ones have difficulty understanding him. Through the VOICE trial, Terry is using his Neuralink implant to help fine-tune a brain-to-voice interface for himself and others who can’t speak.”

bullets.section: Small fitness tool I still use and love
bullets.title: Tune Up Fitness – Alpha Ball
bullets.creator: Tune Up Fitness
bullets.note: This was recommended to me by [Nsima Inyang](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mLGqrlxofXQ), a mutant among mutants. The Alpha Ball solves a few different problems at the same time: (1) It’s precise. Foam rollers are big, amorphous objects. It can be hard to get them to certain spots (e.g., hips—TFL, glute medius, piriformis), which the Alpha Ball can easily access. (2) It’s compact enough for luggage and travel. This also means I can use it against a wall for spinal erectors, rear of the shoulders, etc. (3) It has a Goldilocks density: not too hard and not too soft. The firmness hits the sweet spot—hard enough to work out deep knots but not so aggressive that it causes excessive pain or bracing.

bullets.title: Aerolamp
bullets.creator: Aerolamp
bullets.note: I recently purchased multiple [Jaspr](https://jaspr.co/products/airscrubber) air purifiers, so I’m not rushing to buy any other air-filtration tools, but far-UVC is fascinating, and I’m learning more. This lamp uses light to inactivate airborne viruses and bacteria and is designed for use while people are in the room. In a [published study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-57441-z), four ceiling-mounted far-UVC fixtures reduced infectious airborne mouse norovirus by 99.8%. Adam Strandberg, a researcher at Harvard’s [Needleman Lab](https://needleman.seas.harvard.edu/) who works on bacterial respiratory control, added one in his living room and [hosted his kid’s birthday party with no disease transmission](https://x.com/strandbergbio/status/2101839595004469395).
